patients.summary: Licensed practical nurse with recurrent depression, chronic migraine, IBS-D and quiescent epilepsy who joins in 2020; later factitious diarrhea and surreptitious sulfonylurea hypoglycemia lead to a diagnosis of factitious disorder imposed on self. Toxic epidermal necrolysis from lamotrigine in 2024, three episodes of serotonin syndrome 2025 to 2026, and a pregnancy ending in severe preeclampsia with pulmonary edema and preterm cesarean in January 2026.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish with the practice. Works as an LPN at a rehab facility, says her old office in town is closing its doors to adult patients at the end of the year. Membership terms reviewed, she will sign at the first visit. Booked new patient appt 9/17 at 2:40. Signed release sent by email; we will fax the request to her prior primary care office for the last 5 yrs of notes, labs and immunizations.

documents.title: Prior primary care office records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office, 38 pages, covering 2015 to 2020.

Problem summary as carried by that office: depression, recurrent, on sertraline since her early twenties with good response at 100 mg; migraine without aura, chronic, uses sumatriptan; IBS with diarrhea predominance, loperamide as needed; epilepsy, onset in adolescence, followed in childhood by pediatric neurology, seizure-free for many years and off antiseizure medicine since her late teens.

Surgical: laparoscopic appendectomy 2015, uneventful recovery.
Allergy: sulfa antibiotics - rash.

Last Pap 2018 NILM. Childhood vaccines documented complete. Influenza vaccine yearly through her employer.

Most recent visit 03/2020: PHQ-9 of 6, BP 112/70, weight 63 kg. No labs in the last 12 months.

conditions.label: Epilepsy
conditions.note: Seizure-free for years, off antiseizure medication

Take 1 capsule by mouth as needed for loose stools. Max 8 mg per day

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29F here to establish. LPN, works days at a rehab and skilled nursing facility. Married, no kids. Prior office records reviewed (scanned 9/14).

Depression: recurrent, first episode in her early 20s. On sertraline 100 mg for years, feels it works. Mood 'okay, work is a lot right now.' No SI. Not in counseling at present. PHQ-9 7, GAD-7 5.

Migraine: chronic, no aura. Mother has the same. Uses sumatriptan 100, usually works within an hour. Estimates 6 to 8 doses a month. Discussed medication-overuse headache and prevention; she would rather keep things as they are for now.

IBS-D: years of loose stools with stress, loperamide a few times a month. No blood, no weight loss, no nocturnal stools. Sister has IBS too.

Epilepsy: seizures as a teenager, treated in childhood, off meds since about age 18 and seizure-free since. Does drive. Maternal aunt has epilepsy.

PSH: lap appy 2015.
FHx: mother depression and migraine; maternal aunt epilepsy; father HTN; sister IBS.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs.
Allergy: sulfa (rash).

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. Vitals as charted. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars. No edema. Neuro: CN intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait normal. Affect a little flat but appropriate.

A/P
1. MDD, recurrent - stable on sertraline 100 mg, will take over prescribing. Counseling list given.
2. Chronic migraine without aura - sumatriptan PRN; headache diary. Revisit prevention if frequency climbs.
3. IBS-D - loperamide PRN.
4. Epilepsy, in long remission off meds - no action.
5. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH; HIV and hep C screen once, she agrees. Pap due 2021. Flu shot next month at our nurse clinic (she usually gets it at work, will do it here this year).
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Karen - everything from Thursday came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are all in the normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Talk soon.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before her shift for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reaction to flu shots. Allergy list reviewed (sulfa). Quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 min, fine. Left for work.

documents.title: Sertraline refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: last refill from her prior doctor used up. Sertraline 100 mg #90 with 3 refills sent per PCP plan from the new patient visit.

documents.title: COVID vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Work offered me the COVID shot and I got the first one on the 6th. Anything I should know with my sertraline or my migraines?

documents.title: RE: COVID vaccine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No interaction with sertraline. A headache the day after is common; your usual sumatriptan is fine to use. Please send a picture of your card once you have both doses so we can add it here.

documents.title: Employer vaccination card
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pt uploaded a photo of her vaccine card from the employee clinic at work: Pfizer COVID-19 doses on 1/6/21 and 1/27/21. Entered into the immunization record. She had a sore arm and a tired day after dose 2, nothing more.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6 mo f/u. Winter was long, worked a lot of extra shifts, but mood held. Taking sertraline daily. PHQ-9 6. Headache diary: about 7 migraine days in March, each responded to one sumatriptan. Bowels at her usual, loperamide maybe twice a month.
O: vitals as charted, looks well. Brief exam unremarkable.
A/P: MDD recurrent - stable, continue sertraline 100. Chronic migraine - stable on PRN triptan, reminded of the 2-day-a-week ceiling to avoid rebound. IBS-D quiet. Physical and Pap in the fall.

documents.title: Sumatriptan quantity limit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurer limits sumatriptan to 9 tabs per 30 days. Her prior office prescription has run out. New Rx sent for #9 with refills under our name; PA for quantity not needed at this amount, she says 9 is usually enough. Loperamide also rewritten so it is on our list (she buys it OTC most months).

documents.title: Physical scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to set up her yearly physical with Pap. Booked 10/19 8:20, reminded to come in fasting is not needed.

reports.text: Specimen: liquid-based cervical cytology with high-risk HPV co-test. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit, age 30.

Interval: no new issues. Mood steady, PHQ-9 5. Migraines about the same, 6 to 8 a month, triptan works. IBS flares with stress, loperamide occasionally. No seizures. Not planning a pregnancy at present; discussed folic acid if that changes.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well appearing. Skin without rashes. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts symmetric, no masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap and HPV collected. Extremities without edema. Neuro nonfocal. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap with HPV today. Tdap (last one over 10 yrs ago per old records) and flu today. CBC/CMP.
- MDD, migraine, IBS-D: unchanged, meds continued.
RTC 6 months or as needed.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap smear was normal and the HPV test was negative, so the next one is not due for five years. Blood work from the physical was normal too.
